thread:
vikram: Heads-up: Europulse reported they were billed in USD instead of EUR for invoice INV-2026-0783. They were charged conversion fees by their bank and want us to refund the FX delta.
sasha: Can you pull the invoice? We should have a EUR billing flag on the account.
ovar: (typo) sorry, meant to tag @omar
omar: Pulled it. Account had `currency=EUR` in profile, but invoice generation service defaulted to USD due to a region-mapping bug for EU customers created before 2026-01-01. Invoice shows $1,200. Converted at customer's bank rate they paid €1,088. Expected EUR invoice should have been €1,050 (platform EUR pricing), so customer overpaid ~€38 plus bank fee €7 = €45.
vikram: Small amount but it's an ops error, we should credit the FX delta and a small goodwill for the bank fee. Total request €45.
elaine: I can approve up to €500 in EUR-equivalent. Approved. Please tag reason `goodwill: fx_misinvoice` and include invoice id.
sasha: Will create manual credit. Note our ledger is in USD so we need USD equivalent. Using our rate table 2026-03-12: 1 EUR = 1.103 USD => €45 = $49.64 round to $49.64.
omar: Command I run:
```
# credit for EUR misinvoice + bank fee
billingctl credit --customer EURO-41 --invoice INV-2026-0783 --amount 49.64 --currency USD --reason "goodwill: fx_misinvoice" --note "customer saw EUR invoice; refund €45"
```
billing-bot: Credit created: cr_1N9fQ3Dy, amount $49.64, status: pending.
vikram: I'll send the customer the explanation + confirmation of the €45 credit and attach revised invoice PDF in EUR. CC’ing accounts.
elaine: Added to March manual adjustments sheet under EUR corrections. Also opened ENG ticket ENG-4088 to fix region-mapping.
sasha: Customer replied in thread  thanks, appreciated the quick fix
